stage.quote: The company today announced it raised a $3.5 million seed round led by Tiger Global, with additional investment from Y Combinator, Charge Ventures, Uncorrelated Ventures, Twenty Two Ventures and Soma Capital, along with angels including Guy Podjarny and Jason Warner.
stage.note: Round was raised in 2022 under the company's original name/product, Slai (same founders Eli Mernit and Luke Lombardi, same investor set later listed on beam.cloud/about: Tiger Global, Charge Ventures, Soma Capital, Y Combinator). Slai was rebranded to Beam (beam.cloud) as an open-source serverless/sandbox GPU cloud. No priced round after the 2022 seed was found in ~15 min of research (no TechCrunch/press hits, no blog announcement); YC's own profile still lists the company as a 5-person team, consistent with no larger follow-on round. Beam's own about page additionally shows Alumni Ventures and Hustle Fund logos (and NVIDIA Inception Program membership, which is a partner program, not an investor), which could indicate a later seed extension/additional seed investors not covered by a dedicated press article; treated as part of the same seed stage absent a differently-dated/priced round.

note: Beam (beam.cloud) is the rebrand of Slai, an ML-deployment platform founded in 2021 by Eli Mernit and Luke Lombardi, YC W22 (Active per YC directory), same domain/founders confirmed against the YC hint. The only confirmed funding event found is Slai's May-2022 $3.5M seed led by Tiger Global with YC, Charge Ventures, Uncorrelated Ventures, Twenty Two Ventures, Soma Capital and angels Guy Podjarny and Jason Warner (TechCrunch). Beam's own about page lists Tiger Global, Y Combinator, Charge Ventures, Soma Capital, Alumni Ventures and Hustle Fund as backers, and separately touts NVIDIA Inception Program membership (a technology partner program, not a funding round). No later priced round (seed extension, Series A, etc.) or revenue/ARR figure was found in the ~15-minute research window; buyers should treat total funding and stage as likely stale given the company has clearly grown its product surface (GPU cloud, sandboxes, inference) well beyond the original 2022 ML-deployment tool.
